dining-room.definition: A room mainly used for eating meals at a table.
dining-room.exampleUsage: The dining room is beside the kitchen.

home-office.definition: A room or designated area in a private residence set aside mainly for administrative, professional, or academic work. It commonly contains a desk, computer, and storage for documents and other materials.

laundry-room.definition: A room or area equipped for washing and drying clothes.
laundry-room.exampleUsage: The laundry room has a washer and dryer.

basement.definition: The ground floor facade or interior in Renaissance architecture.

attic.definition: Of or relating to Attica or its inhabitants or to the dialect spoken in Athens in classical times.

pantry.definition: A small storeroom for storing foods or wines.

backyard.definition: The grounds in back of a house.

front-yard.definition: The outdoor area on the street-facing side of a house is its front yard.

patio.definition: Usually paved outdoor area adjoining a residence.

deck.definition: A porch that resembles the deck on a ship.

balcony.definition: An upper floor projecting from the rear over the main floor in an auditorium.

terrace.definition: A row of houses built in a similar style and having common dividing walls (or the street on which they face).

porch.definition: A structure attached to the exterior of a building often forming a covered entrance.

gazebo.definition: A small roofed structure in a park where people can rest.

pergola.definition: A framework that supports climbing plants.

garden-shed.definition: A small building used for storing garden tools.

fireplace.definition: An open recess in a wall at the base of a chimney where a fire can be built.

walk-in-closet.definition: A large closet designed so a person can step inside to access clothing and storage.
walk-in-closet.exampleUsage: The bedroom includes a walk-in closet.

built-in-shelves.definition: Shelves constructed as a permanent part of a wall or room.

crown-molding.definition: Decorative trim fitted along the upper edge where a wall meets the ceiling.
crown-molding.exampleUsage: Crown molding runs around the living-room ceiling.

hardwood-floor.definition: A floor made from solid or engineered wood with a visible wood surface.
hardwood-floor.exampleUsage: The living room has a hardwood floor.

tile-floor.definition: A floor covered with individual tiles made from materials such as ceramic, porcelain, or stone.
tile-floor.exampleUsage: The kitchen has an easy-to-clean tile floor.

vaulted-ceiling.definition: A high ceiling that slopes or arches upward instead of remaining flat.
vaulted-ceiling.exampleUsage: The vaulted ceiling makes the room feel more open.

skylight.definition: A window in a roof to admit daylight.

bay-window.definition: A window structure that extends beyond the main wall of a house.

french-doors.definition: A pair of doors with large glass panes extending through much of their height.
french-doors.exampleUsage: French doors open from the living room to the patio.

hvac.definition: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems used to control indoor temperature and air movement.
hvac.exampleUsage: The HVAC system was serviced before summer.

central-air.definition: A system that cools or heats air in a central unit and distributes it through ducts around a building.
central-air.exampleUsage: The house uses central air throughout the rooms.

furnace.definition: An enclosed chamber in which heat is produced to heat buildings, destroy refuse, smelt or refine ores, etc.

water-heater.definition: An appliance that heats and holds water so it is ready for household use.

plumbing.definition: Utility consisting of the pipes and fixtures for the distribution of water or gas in a building and for the disposal of sewage.

electrical-panel.definition: A cabinet in a building contains switches or fuses that regulate electricity and protect individual circuits from damage.

circuit-breaker.definition: An automatic safety switch that cuts off electricity when an overload or short circuit threatens to damage the wiring.

thermostat.definition: To control the temperature with a thermostat.

septic-tank.definition: A large tank treats household wastewater by using bacteria to break down its solid waste.

well-water.definition: Water obtained by pumping a well that reaches underground water, for drinking or other household needs.
